page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built for balanced compute and memory requirements. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs using dedicated CPU allocation with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 ratio of compute threads to memory capacity.

This server instance does not include integrated local storage and operates without discrete hardware GPU accelerators. Persistent data handling requires network-attached block volumes. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated CPU assignment eliminates multi-tenant noisy-neighbor interference and performance throttling found in burstable instances, delivering consistent instruction processing across sustained operational periods.

The absence of onboard NVMe drives reflects an architectural emphasis on compute and RAM balance rather than high-IOPS local scratch space. VM.Standard3.Flex.4-32 is suitable for standard enterprise backends, web serving tiers, application container hosting, microservices, and continuous integration and continuous delivery execution environments.
